name: Tanpura
description: Four-string Indian drone lute: a held key is plucked round and round, and each pluck blooms into a slow sweep of overtones as the string grazes its curved bridge.

params.name: Tuning
params.description: The first string against the key: Pa a fourth below it, Ma a fifth below, Ni a semitone below. The other three stay on the key and its lower octave.

params.name: Jawari
params.description: How firmly the curved bridge holds the string. At zero it is a plain string; higher makes each pluck open into a longer, louder sweep of buzzing overtones.

params.name: Speed
params.description: Time for one round of the four plucks. Short is a busy shimmer; long lets each string ring down before it is plucked again.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long each string rings after its pluck. Applies from each string's next pluck.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Tunes the two middle strings apart so they beat slowly against each other. Applies from each string's next pluck.

params.name: Body
params.description: Blend from the bare strings to the hollow gourd they sit on, which adds a low woody resonance.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places the four strings across the stereo field. At zero all four sit in the centre.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit after the tanpura, the four-string drone lute of Indian classical music. Each string is a stiff digital waveguide loop (Karplus-Strong and Jaffe-Smith lineage) at twice the sample rate whose bridge end is a jawari, modelled as a lossless junction: where the wave swings onto the bridge it turns round a little early, and the short piece of string behind the contact point is cut off until the string lifts again. The two-point picture of the bridge and the need for a stiff string follow what is recalled of Raman (1921), Valette, and van Walstijn and Chatziioannou's tanpura simulations; no page of them was read for this work, the reduced junction is our own, and it is checked only by measurement: a delayed bloom of the upper partials, Raman's missing-partial test, level dependence, a band of overtones that slides down, pitch, and passivity. Simplified: one polarisation, no coupling between the strings through the bridge, no tension modulation, a gourd of five fixed resonances, and the plucking finger as a short damping before each pluck. Choices rather than measurements of an instrument: the inharmonicity (2e-5), the length of string behind the contact point (0.5 % of the period), the contact gap and reach, the softness of the pluck, the shape of the decay, the body resonances and the stereo places. Nobody has listened to it beside a real tanpura. Not a circuit or sample emulation.
